decisions.statement: A parts list is sorted by the whole `type/slug` a part is written as.
A slug is read under the page type written with it rather than on its own.
Two parts spelled alike are in order either way round.
A refusal names the first pair out of order rather than every pair.
Every page the change carries is judged rather than a page of one type.
A page naming no part is passed over.
A page the change takes away is passed over.
A page whose body will not load is passed over.
`page-matches-its-type` refuses a body that will not load.
Nothing is judged while this page states `experimental`.
`experimental` comes off this page where Alan has approved this check.
A part is put into a parts list in the order that list is sorted by.
`parts` says it is sorted, and `add-property-value` reads that off the shape.

definition: the check refusing a page naming its parts out of order
